nt2e41.title: First scarf day
nt2e41.caption:
Leo walked out in slow motion for the first scarf of winter. The scarf had other plans, and so did Libra.
Who in your life would happily share a scarf?

nt2e42.title: The window seat
nt2e42.caption:
Rain on the glass, deep thoughts, a whole movie in Cancer's head. Then the bus kept going.
Ever missed your stop and found something better?

nt2e43.title: The dropped book
nt2e43.caption:
Gemini dropped the book for the big meet-cute. Virgo reached for it with their own title card ready.
Two main characters, one café. Who gets top billing?

nt2e44.title: Catching the train
nt2e44.caption:
Sagittarius sprinted for the last train like the credits were rolling. The doors had opinions. Aquarius did not let them win.
Who holds the door for you?

nt2e45.title: Tears in the snow
nt2e45.caption:
Pisces wanted one perfect tear in the first snow. It froze and went clink. Scorpio showed up with a tissue and cocoa anyway.
Tag the friend who brings the cocoa.

nt2e46.title: A first date, explained badly
nt2e46.caption:
Virgo's whiteboard breakdown of a first date: two strangers, one table, snacks, and two people insisting they're chill.
What would you add to the diagram?

nt2e47.title: A crush, explained badly
nt2e47.caption:
Capricorn explains a crush with a marker and zero chill: a tab opens in your brain and it simply never closes.
How long have you re-read one text?

nt2e48.title: Cuffing season, explained badly
nt2e48.caption:
Aquarius explains cuffing season with penguins, which honestly tracks. The blanket is optional. The person is the point.
Team blanket or team person?

nt2e49.title: Meeting the parents, explained badly
nt2e49.caption:
Gemini says meeting the parents is a job interview with lasagna and your baby photos on a slideshow. Then the twist: they're nervous too.
What did you bring the first time?

nt2e50.title: A talk card, explained badly
nt2e50.caption:
Taurus explains a talk card: it asks a question, you both answer honestly, and somehow it tastes like dessert.
Which question would you want to draw first?

nt2e51.title: Late to the date
nt2e51.caption:
Sagittarius ran late and the couch is scoring the excuses. A dog needing directions tops out at 6. The scenic route gets a 2. The honest one gets the room.
What's the best excuse you've heard?

nt2e52.title: The slow reply
nt2e52.caption:
A day to text back, and Aquarius has excuses: the other jacket, a draft that became a novel. The couch only perks up for the truth.
Would you take the honest answer?

nt2e53.title: Skipping the party
nt2e53.caption:
Capricorn tried "a meeting with my couch" and a calendar that just says NAP. Then came the real answer, with a dinner plan attached.
Party person or dinner-for-two person?

nt2e54.title: Not dancing
nt2e54.caption:
Leo won't dance because the shoes are too iconic and the floor isn't ready. The couch is unmoved until Leo admits the real reason.
Who would you ask to teach you?

nt2e55.title: Not saying it yet
nt2e55.caption:
Scorpio blamed the signs and the moon for not saying "I like you." The couch wanted the truth, and the truth got the best reply.
What finally made you say it?

nt2e56.title: Snack paused
nt2e56.caption:
It's 1 AM and Taurus is drafting sandwich questions and snack-sharing vows. The one they send is simpler, and it works.
What's on your 1 AM drafts list?

nt2e57.title: Alphabetised
nt2e57.caption:
Virgo at 1 AM: a sorted shelf, a label maker, and two drafts too clever by half. The plain one gets the smile.
Do you overthink the late text too?

nt2e58.title: Sunrise plan
nt2e58.caption:
Aries at 1 AM went straight to all caps. The text they actually sent was a sunrise plan, and the reply came back fast.
Who would answer your 1 AM idea?

nt2e59.title: Sorry, moon
nt2e59.caption:
Libra drafted a moon poll at 1 AM, deleted it, and said the sweet thing instead. The moon took the news well.
Have you ever blamed the moon for a feeling?

nt2e60.title: Say it at noon
nt2e60.caption:
Scorpio, hood up, deletes two drafts and then just says it. The reply asks for a repeat in daylight.
Would you say it again at noon?
